voice_note: LAB-2212: one line per chapter, read by OpenAI TTS (tts.py). Chapter length = narration + pauses. Opening (owner 11-02): the chorus coding post first, no app until 'started'.

lines.hook: An agent that gets each step right ninety-nine percent of the time finishes a fifty-step task correctly only sixty-one percent of the time. Handing everything to one agent, and walking away, doesn't work.
lines.chorus: So I work with a chorus of agents. Several coding agents on the same work, each doing the part it does best, and one checking another. I call it chorus coding.
lines.reasons: One agent can't do it all, for four reasons. Cost: most work doesn't need the most expensive model. Capacity: one subscription runs out. Quality: different agents are best at different jobs. And independent checks: an agent shouldn't grade its own work.
lines.started: It started on a Friday in October. Twenty-two terminal tabs, five windows, one laptop. Every tab looked the same, agents sat waiting for answers, and context got lost. So I built a roof over my agents.
lines.home: This is One Roof. Start the day on Home. It reads the night for you: which loops ran, what failed, and what to do next, before you open a single terminal.
lines.windows: All windows is the heart of it. Every window, every session, and a live feed of what each agent finished, found, or got stuck on.
lines.inbox: Everything the agents ask you lands in one Inbox, the urgent ones first. Each agent's own options become buttons. One click answers, and nothing is ever approved for you.
lines.session: Each session is the real agent, in a real terminal. Claude works through its plan, and you can always type straight into it.
lines.newsession: Starting a session takes seconds. Pick the agent and the account, the Linear project and the issue, and say what done looks like.
lines.projects: That's the method. You plan in Linear, and you execute here, with many kinds of agents. Tickets come in, sessions go out, and the results are written back. No spreadsheets.
lines.resources: Even two or three agents can clog a laptop. Resources shows what every session and every app is using, what's hanging, and lets you act on it right here.
lines.loops: Loops run on their own, with the app open or closed. About twenty-five come ready to run: to watch, check, improve and report, each with its own limits and gates.
lines.learn: There is a lot to learn. Learn organizes it around context, loops, evidence and procedure, and the people worth hearing. Every card is narrated, so it keeps playing while you work.
lines.evals: Evals is still a draft. It goes beyond benchmarks: it helps you measure your own agents, on your own work, with questions built from your repo's real bugs.
lines.history: And History keeps the important moments of every session, so you always know what happened while you were away.
lines.end: One Roof. Many coding agents, one place to keep up, and you stay in charge. Free and open source.
